## Wave 2 — the Valley meshes (Ben, 2026-10-02)

Ben's first Studio look at wave 1 (one screenshot, no complaint): "we didnt do step A2 yet? do
it". Rulings:

1. **The whole A2 Valley in one wave** (the old waves 2 and 3 together): mountains, foothills,
   forest, waterfall, far hills, the ground with its patches and baked roads, river, pond, lake,
   bridges, stepping stones, groves, aprons, clouds. One upload batch, **one harvest paste**.
2. The look reference is the mock's A2 renders (`out/A2_*.png`, `wm_valley2.py`,
   `out/A2_numbers.json`), with two changes the lead announced: **aprons are light era gravel in
   two flat bands** (the dark base colour bleeding outward read as scorch marks), and no signposts
   (each plot already has its Sign).

### Principles

- **Collision stays flat and made of Parts.** The `Ground` Part at Y = −`plotSize.Y` stays the
  only floor, visible, in the meadow green. Every mesh is visual: `Anchored`, with `CanCollide`,
  `CanQuery` and `CanTouch` false. Nothing depends on a MeshPart's collision geometry.
- **So the walkable basin is flat.** Inside the wall the visual ground never rises more than
  `overlayLift` above the Ground Part. The 1-stud kerb at the plot edges stays (no visual ramp:
  feet would sink into it). The river is not carved: its bed is coloured faces in the ground
  overlay and its water is a translucent sheet `water.lift` above the ground, so a player wades
  ankle-deep on the flat floor.
- **What collides, as server Parts built from data:** the wall, each bridge (deck and two ramps)
  and each stepping stone. These are world structures, a category next to client dressing; the
  M9 rule "no dressing part collides" is unchanged.
- **One source of truth for geometry: the generator.** A Python tool derives everything from the
  ring and writes both the meshes and `src/shared/Config/Valley.json`. Luau reads that data and
  never recomputes the river, the bridges or the wall. (`WorldPlan` keeps only the ring and the
  wave 1 roads.)
- **Baked for one `plotCount`.** The meshes fit the ring they were generated for. `Valley.json`
  records `plotCount`; if it differs from the live ring, the server warns once and builds the
  wave 1 look. When `m11-unlocks` (6 plots) merges, the Valley is regenerated and re-uploaded:
  one more harvest paste.
- **Everything degrades to wave 1.** No `Valley.json`, no `ServerStorage.Assets.World.Valley`, a
  `plotCount` mismatch, or a missing **required** mesh → the wave 1 world, with one warning. A
  missing optional mesh is left out, named in one warning.
- **Levels stay frozen** (wave 1). The skirt band around each plot stays at ground level.

### Frames

- **World frame** (`"frame": "world"`): X and Z are Roblox world studs (plot `i` centre at
  `(cos, sin)(angle_i) · radius`); generator Y = 0 is the **ground top**. The server places a world
  mesh with `PivotTo(CFrame.new(0, -plotSize.Y, 0))`.
- **Plot frame** (`"frame": "plot"`): the plot's local frame, origin at the plot centre, −Z toward
  the hub, generator Y = 0 at the ground top. One template, cloned once per plot with
  `PivotTo(base.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, -plotSize.Y / 2, 0))`.
- Blender is Z-up: Blender `(x, y, z)` is glTF/Roblox `(x, z, −y)`. A sign slip mirrors the
  valley; the preview gate below exists to catch it.
- 1 glTF unit = 1 stud, no scale anywhere. A template places a mesh at its generator coordinates
  with its facing preserved (verified on all 94 Village path meshes).

### The generator — `tools/world/valley.py` (landscape-builder)

```
py tools/world/valley.py build            # GLBs, palette, bake record, Valley.json
py tools/world/valley.py check            # QA gate: committed Valley.json == a fresh build
py tools/world/valley.py build --count 6 --out-root <scratch> --data <scratch>/Valley.json
```

- Reads `Game.json` (`plotCount`, `plotMargin`, `hubRadius`), the Village layout's `plotSize`,
  `World.json` (road width, colours it shares with wave 1) and its own art numbers in
  `tools/world/Valley.plan.json` (palette, noise, river widths, densities). The ring comes from
  `tools/worldplan.py`, a line-for-line mirror of `WorldPlan.Ring` with a `selftest` (277.0217
  and 183.9230).
- Writes, under the shared `assets/build/world/`: `Valley/<Mesh>.glb`, `Valley/palette.png`,
  `Valley.json` (the bake record). Writes `src/shared/Config/Valley.json` in the worktree.
- **Deterministic.** Two `build` runs give byte-identical GLBs, PNG and JSON (seeded noise, the
  pure-Python GLB writer of `tools/paths/planargeom.py`, no Blender exporter). It may run under
  `py` or under Blender's bundled Python (for numpy), like `tools/paths/texture.py`.
- **GLB shape:** one scene, one node, one mesh, **one primitive, no material, no image**:
  `POSITION`, per-face `NORMAL`, `TEXCOORD_0`, uint32 indices. Front faces are counter-clockwise
  seen from outside; nothing is double-sided. A flat sheet gets a hair of height (the importer
  rejects a zero-height bounding box).
- **Colour:** a `palette` mesh maps each face's UVs to the centre of its colour's swatch in
  `palette.png` (16-px swatches, opaque, one PNG for the whole set). A `flat` mesh has one colour,
  set on the MeshPart by the template or at runtime, and no texture.
- **Hard limits, asserted at build:** ≤ 20,000 triangles per mesh (aim ≤ 18,000); every bounding
  box side ≤ 1,500 studs; terrain outer radius ≤ 1,600; mesh names `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, ≤ 24
  characters; ≤ 32 meshes in the set.

Mesh set (names are a guide; the builder may split or merge within the limits):

| Mesh | Frame | Look | Required | Contents |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Basin_<k>` | world | palette | yes | the flat ground overlay inside the foothills at `overlayLift`: two-tone meadow, darker and wildflower patches, the earth ring, the bent dirt roads with rims, river and pond bed, banks, sand; holes under the hub and the plots are not needed (they sit above it) |
| `Details` | world | palette | no | stepping stones, hub kerb and bollards, flowers and tufts |
| `Groves` | world | palette | no | the tree clumps between the roads |
| `Water` | world | flat | no | river, pond and lake surface, translucent |
| `Bridge_<n>` | world | palette | no | plank deck, ramps and rails, one mesh per bridge |
| `Foothills_<k>`, `Mountains_<k>`, `FarHills_<k>` | world | palette | no | terrain outside the wall, rock and snow lines as in A2, the lake shore |
| `Forest_<k>` | world | palette | no | generated pines on the foothills |
| `Waterfall` | world | palette | no | the two-tier fall above the river's source |
| `Clouds` | world | flat | no | the flat low-poly clusters |
| `ApronInner`, `ApronOuter` | plot | flat | no | two flat bands around a plot, irregular outer edge, 16–40 studs reach where the wedge has room; clipped to the plot's own sector (0.3 studs short of the bisector, so neighbours never overlap) and cut open for the road corridor; `ApronOuter` lies outside `ApronInner`, never under it |
| `Entrance` | plot | palette | no | two short fence runs flanking the road at the plot's front edge |

- Roads bend gently as in A2 and still end at the centre of each plot's front edge (plot-local
  `(0, −plotSize.Z / 2)`) and at the hub. The river uses the mock's gaps (it enters between plot
  N and plot 1 and leaves after plot `round(N / 2) + 1`), widths and pond.
- Stacking above the ground top, so no two visible faces are coplanar: `overlayLift` 0.10 (basin),
  aprons 0.16, water `water.lift` 0.35, bridge deck 0.70. Trees, stones and fences start at the
  overlay.
- Trees, fences, stones and bridges are generated geometry in the set's palette (colours sampled
  from the Village kits so they sit with the skirt woods). No kit GLB is baked in.

### `Valley.json` — generated data (`src/shared/Config/Valley.json`, never hand-edited)

Heights are studs above the ground top. `yaw` is radians about +Y, 0 = the bridge's long axis
along +X, turning toward +Z.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "plotCount": 10,
  "ringRadius": 277.0217,
  "planHash": "9c1f0a7e2b6d4c35",
  "overlayLift": 0.1,
  "wallRadius": 358.3,
  "meshes": [
    { "name": "Basin_1", "frame": "world", "required": true },
    { "name": "ApronInner", "frame": "plot", "tint": "apronInner" },
    { "name": "ApronOuter", "frame": "plot", "tint": "apronOuter" }
  ],
  "bridges": [
    { "x": -141.9, "z": -98.6, "yaw": 0.61, "length": 23.7, "width": 7, "deckTop": 0.7, "deckThickness": 0.5, "rampLength": 3.5 }
  ],
  "stones": [ { "x": 0, "z": -67, "radius": 1.75, "top": 0.62 } ],
  "river": [ [221.0, -71.8, 5.5] ]
}
```

- `meshes`: every template to place, in order. `required` (default false). `tint` (plot frame
  only): the mesh is recoloured per plot from `World.json valley.aprons` by the plot's era.
- `bridges`: `length` is the deck (ramps add `rampLength` at each end); the deck's top is at
  `deckTop` and the ramps fall from it to the ground top.
- `stones`: an upright cylinder each, top at `top`.
- `river`: channel samples `[x, z, halfWidth]` in world studs along the centreline, pond included,
  from the wall inward only. It exists for the client's skirt rule below. `halfWidth` covers the
  visible water plus its bank.

### `World.json` additions (lead-applied)

```json
"valley": {
  "wall": { "height": 160, "thickness": 4, "segments": 36 },
  "aprons": {
    "Village": { "inner": [114, 142, 66], "outer": [120, 149, 71] },
    "Boomtown": { "inner": [178, 160, 102], "outer": [152, 158, 89] },
    "Metropolis": { "inner": [150, 150, 144], "outer": [138, 153, 110] },
    "OrbitalColony": { "inner": [136, 134, 138], "outer": [131, 145, 107] }
  },
  "skirtMargin": 1.5
}
```

- `wall`: `segments` flat invisible Parts in a ring, their inner faces tangent to
  `Valley.json wallRadius`, standing from the ground top to `height`, `thickness` deep.
- `aprons.<EraName>`: `inner` and `outer` colours (`outer` is halfway to the meadow). An era with
  no entry hides both bands.
- `skirtMargin`: extra studs around the river channel in the client's skirt rule.

### Pipeline — a copy of the baked-paths route (pipeline-engineer)

The props route is not used (it needs kits, blueprints, a Blender join and has no hash).

- `tools/assets/assets_config.py`: a `world` block that `render_assets` serialises (today unknown
  top-level keys are erased on the next save). Shape, key order fixed like `render_path_era`:
  ```json
  "world": { "Valley": {
    "plotCount": 10, "planHash": "9c1f0a7e2b6d4c35", "triangles": 103084,
    "paletteAssetId": 0, "paletteImageId": 0, "paletteSha256": "",
    "meshes": { "Basin_1": {
      "assetId": 0, "meshId": 0, "size": [0, 0, 0], "offset": [0, 0, 0], "sha256": "",
      "triangles": 17500, "look": "palette" },
      "Water": { "assetId": 0, "meshId": 0, "size": [0, 0, 0], "offset": [0, 0, 0], "sha256": "",
      "triangles": 900, "look": "flat", "color": [58, 144, 200], "transparency": 0.25 } } } }
  ```
- `tools/assets/upload_world.py` (new), modelled on `upload_paths.py`: reads the bake record,
  uploads each GLB as a Model and the palette as a Decal, sha256 skip, `Assets.json` saved after
  every upload, resumable, the 50-character display-name guard (`EraCityTycoon_World_<Set>_<Mesh>`
  else `ECT_World_…`), `--only <Mesh>` for the trial upload, `--dry-run` that writes **nothing**,
  and the scratch flags (`--assets-json`, `--bake-root`). Meshes no longer in the bake record are
  dropped. The palette PNG check: opaque, any size.
- `tools/assets/harvest.py`: kinds `worldMesh` and `worldTexture` ride along with whichever paste
  comes next, like the path kinds (the Decal branch must accept `worldTexture`). `merge` requires
  exactly one MeshPart per mesh and **checks the harvested `size` against the bake record's**
  (tolerance 0.01 studs or 0.1%): a mismatch means the importer rescaled the mesh; it is reported
  per mesh and exits non-zero after merging the rest.
- `tools/assets/gen_templates.py`: `--world`, `GROUP_DIRNAMES["world"] = "_world"`, and the world
  tree in `--check`. Output `templates/_world/<Set>/<Mesh>.rbxmx` (two levels, so a branch
  without this change never mistakes it for an era folder): a `Model "<Mesh>"`, `WorldPivot`
  identity, one MeshPart `Mesh` with `Anchored` true, `CanCollide`/`CanQuery`/`CanTouch` false,
  `CastShadow` false, `CollisionFidelity` Box, `RenderFidelity` Precise, `Material`
  SmoothPlastic, `harvested_cframe` with lift 0. `palette`: white, `TextureContent` = the palette
  image. `flat`: `Color3uint8` = `color`, `Transparency` = `transparency`, no texture.
- `tools/gen_asset_manifest.py`: a "World" table (set, meshes, triangles, uploaded/templated).
- The bake record (`assets/build/world/Valley.json`), written by the generator, read by the
  uploader and by harvest:
  ```json
  { "set": "Valley", "plotCount": 10, "ringRadius": 277.0217, "planHash": "9c1f0a7e2b6d4c35",
    "palette": { "file": "Valley/palette.png", "sha256": "…", "size": [112, 96] },
    "meshes": { "Basin_1": { "file": "Valley/Basin_1.glb", "sha256": "…", "triangles": 17500,
      "vertices": 52500, "centre": [0, 0.05, 0], "size": [754.6, 0.11, 754.6],
      "look": "palette" } } }
  ```
  A `flat` mesh adds `"color"` and `"transparency"`.

### Rojo (luau-engineer)

`default.project.json`: add `"templates/_world"` to `globIgnorePaths` and a child
`"World": { "$className": "Folder", "$path": { "optional": "templates/_world" } }` under
`ServerStorage.Assets`. `combat.project.json`: the ignore entry only. No `templates/World` folder
may ever exist (Rojo does not merge an explicit child into a same-named directory).

### Server — `Landscape` (luau-engineer)

- `Catalog.GetValleyPlan(): Types.ValleyPlan?` (nil is the signal) and the `ValleyPlan` types,
  placed like the wave 1 additions. `WorldConfig.valley` types.
- **Mesh mode** when `Valley.json` exists, `ServerStorage.Assets.World.Valley` exists,
  `plotCount` matches the ring and every `required` mesh has a template. Otherwise wave 1, with
  one warning saying which condition failed (no warning when `Valley.json` or the folder is
  simply absent).
- In mesh mode `Landscape.Build`:
  - builds `Ground` and `Hub` as in wave 1, and **no** `HubSurround` and **no** `Road_<i>` (both
    are baked into the basin);
  - clones every world-frame mesh once into `Workspace.Landscape.Valley`;
  - builds `Wall_<k>` (invisible, `CanCollide` true, `CanTouch` false),
    `Bridge_<n>` collision (one deck Part and two `WedgePart` ramps each, invisible) and
    `Stone_<n>` collision (invisible cylinders) under `Workspace.Landscape.Collision`.
- `Landscape.AttachPlot(plotFolder: Folder, base: BasePart): ()`, called by
  `PlotService.buildWorld` once per plot inside its loop (the only PlotService change): in mesh
  mode it clones every plot-frame mesh for that plot into `Workspace.Landscape.Valley` and, for
  `tint` meshes, sets the colour from the plot folder's `EraName` attribute now and on every
  change of it. Outside mesh mode it does nothing.
- All of it runs under the wave 1 boot guard: a failure costs the Valley, never the plots.

### Client — skirt entries in the river (ui-engineer)

Village woods (and any later era's `skirt` entries) stand up to 19 studs past a plot's sides, and
the river runs through two 20-stud gaps. A `skirt` entry whose world position lies within
`halfWidth + valley.skirtMargin` of a `Valley.json river` segment is absent: not drawn, and not
a bird flock centre. A segment's `halfWidth` is the larger of its two ends. A **clump** is also
absent if any of its `quads` lies within that reach plus the fabric's `quarterRadius` (a clump's
trees stand up to 6 studs from its centre).

- New `src/client/City/WorldBlock.luau`: `WorldBlock.Blocked(worldX, worldZ, extraRadius?)`. It
  builds the test lazily from `Catalog.GetValleyPlan()` and `Catalog.GetWorldConfig()`, and only
  once all three hold: the plan exists, its `plotCount` equals the number of plots in
  `Workspace.Plots`, and **`Workspace.Landscape.Valley` exists** (the server's sign that it is
  in mesh mode; in every fallback there is no river and the woods stay). Until then it blocks
  nothing and caches nothing.
- `Fabric.luau` changes only by the hook that asks it, for `skirt` entries only (`syncWild` and
  `SurvivingClumps`, renamed `FlockCentres` in M12 wave 3.2). The wild budgets stay positional: a blocked entry keeps its place in them.
  The file is being edited on `m12-boomtown`: keep the hunks minimal. After that merge, any new
  list that carries `skirt` entries needs the same gate.
- Not mirrored in `tools/cityfabric.py` or `plotrender.py`: the rule depends on where a plot sits
  in the world, which a single-plot render does not have. This is the one sanctioned difference
  between the mirror and the client.

### Gates and order (lead)

1. `valley.py build`, then the builder's preview renders of **the baked GLBs** with back-face
   culling on, from the mock's cameras, on the real ring of plots. The lead compares them with
   `A2_*.png` before anything is uploaded.
2. Announce to the Boomtown session and wait for its ack. Trial: `upload_world.py --only` the
   mesh with the most triangles and the mesh with the largest bounding box (18,000 triangles and
   1,000 studs are both untested through Open Cloud; the largest so far are 12,044 and 61).
3. The batch upload, **one harvest paste** by Ben, `harvest.py` (size check), `gen_templates.py
   --world`, `gen_asset_manifest.py`, `rojo build`.
4. Review, QA, docs.

### Preview gate rulings (lead, 2026-10-02)

The baked GLBs were rendered from the mock's cameras with back-face culling on
(`assets/research/2026-10-01-worldmock/out/sheetV_*.png`, A2 | baked) and accepted. Where the
text above differs, these win:

- **28 meshes, about 132,000 triangles.** `Basin_1..2` (required), `Mountains_1..4` (one per
  world quadrant; each holds foothills, mountains and far hills, so there is no `Foothills_` or
  `FarHills_` mesh), `Forest_1..6`, `Groves`, `Details`, `RiverBed`, `Waterfall`, `Water`,
  `Bridge_1..4`, `Clouds_1..4`, `ApronInner`, `ApronOuter`, `Entrance`.
- **`RiverBed` is new** (palette, world, optional), at 0.22. Both neighbours' aprons reach their
  shared bisector, which in the two river gaps is the river's centreline, so the aprons (0.16)
  lay over the painted bed; `RiverBed` repeats the bed and banks above them there. Stacking is
  now: basin 0.10, aprons 0.16, river bed 0.22, water 0.35, bridge deck 0.70.
- **Terrain ends at radius 1,400** (a quadrant must fit the 1,500-stud box). Clouds stand 900 to
  1,260 studs out for the same reason.
- `wallRadius` is 358.9; the foothills start at 362.3. The tallest summit is 310.5 studs above
  the ground top at radius 722.6.
- `Valley.json` `river` starts at the foothills, 3.4 studs outside the wall. `yaw` is folded into
  (−π/2, π/2]. Positions are rounded to 3 decimals and `yaw` to 4.
- A `--count` scratch build writes the game data to `--data` and the bake record next to it as
  `Valley.bake.json`.
- The trial meshes are `Details` (most triangles) and `Mountains_3` (largest box, 1,444 studs).
- The meadow's facet contrast was halved after the first preview (the mosaic read as a pattern).
- Known and accepted: trees and boulders inside the wall do not collide; a straight seam shows
  where two aprons meet at the inner corners; the terrain's outer edge is visible from high above.

### Review rulings (2026-10-02, roblox-reviewer: no Critical, two Warnings)

Placement, the wall, the bridge decks and wedges, the stones, the aprons, the client rule and the
Rojo mapping were verified against the real templates and data. Taken:

- **Mesh mode also needs the `valley` config and a wall.** No `World.json` or no `valley` block:
  not mesh mode, silently. A `valley.wall` that fails validation: not mesh mode, one warning.
  (Without a wall, players could walk through the foothills and off the ground's edge.)
- **`planHash` ties the data to the meshes.** `Valley.json planHash` must equal
  `Assets.json world.Valley.planHash` (written at upload). The server checks it: a mismatch is one
  warning and the wave 1 world. `valley.py check` checks it too, so a re-bake that was never
  uploaded turns QA red. The hash covers the plan file, the ring, `plotSize` and `World.json`
  `ground`, `hub`, `roads` and `valley.wall.segments`: **changing any of those needs a re-bake, an
  upload and a harvest paste.** Haze, lighting, apron colours, wall height and thickness and
  `skirtMargin` are config-only.
- **A collider is built only when its mesh was placed:** `Bridge_<n>` collision needs the
  `Bridge_<n>` mesh, the stones need `Details`.
- `CanQuery = false` has no effect on a part that collides, so the wall, decks, ramps and stones
  still answer raycasts. Nothing in the hub raycasts; the flags stay as written above.
- `WorldBlock` tests for `Workspace.Landscape.Valley` before it counts the plots.
- **A build that is not the one being uploaded must use `--out-root`.** `assets/build/world` is
  shared by every worktree; a 6-plot bake from another worktree would overwrite this branch's
  bake record.
- Open for the Studio look: `Water` is one large translucent MeshPart, so smoke and dust seen
  across the river may sort wrongly (the fix is splitting it); mountains and clouds have centres
  930 to 1,000 studs out and may be culled at low graphics quality; a skirt tree can stand in the
  river until a plot's next sync if the Valley folder replicates late (accepted).

### Done when (wave 2)

- Studio: the A2 Valley around the ring. Mountains, forest and waterfall behind the plots; the
  river, pond and lake; bridges you walk over and a river you wade through; stepping stones you
  stand on; groves and flower patches in the centre; a light gravel apron around each plot that
  changes with its era; a wall you cannot pass at the foothills. Plots and city dressing are
  unchanged, except that no skirt tree stands in the river.
- With `templates/_world` or `Valley.json` removed: the wave 1 world, no Output error.
- `valley.py check`, `worldplan.py selftest`, `gen_templates.py --check` and
  `gen_asset_manifest.py --check` are green; every existing gate is unchanged and green.

## Wave 4.1 — Orbital growth-layout mock (a gate for Ben, not yet a contract)

Orbital today is Metropolis's lattice with tubes for streets: 16 modules on a 4 × 4 grid, cluster
decking, seven small domes and six rock zones. As for Boomtown and Metropolis, this wave produces
**two candidate layouts**, each a real layout run through the real generator and mirror, so the
pick becomes wave 4.2's starting point with nothing thrown away. Ben's go (2026-10-05): "lets do
it", on the lead's proposal of the candidates "docks" and "axis".

### Facts the candidates work within (measured 2026-10-05)

- **Plot 120** (half 60), fixed. The monorail runs in loop mode on ring 56: its band spans 52.5 to
  59.5 on every side, with no ramp. The beam is 1.6 wide with a soffit at 6.10; each ring cell has
  one pier (foot 1.9 square, 2.5 along the beam from the cell centre). Lots keep 0.5 off the band,
  so they use |x|, |z| ≤ 52. The monorail arrives at purchase 6 (`walkwayNetwork`).
- **Tubes** are tile streets: 7-stud cells on the lattice (7i, 7j), axis-aligned. The pipe is 3.24
  wide (half 1.62) and 1.9 to 2.0 tall. There is no pavement, no walker and no street vehicle. The
  tile meshes: straight 7 × 3.24, end 6.62 × 3.32, bend 5.12 × 5.12, tee 7 × 5.12, cross 7 × 7.
- **Entrance** (0, −49), forced to z ≤ −48.
- **Landmarks** (harvested width × depth, and height by stage 0 to 4). Buy pad 6 × 6.

### What both candidates share

- **Untouched:** the 24 slot ids, their order, config and models
  (`Config/Eras/4_OrbitalColony.json` is frozen); the server, remotes and every Luau file except
  the candidate's own `Layouts/OrbitalColony.luau`; the other eras, whose generated fabric data
  must stay byte-identical.
- **The growth rules of mock B** (CITY_GROWTH §2.5): one heart at the entrance, where the Landing
  Pad (purchase 1) is the seed; slot k roughly k-th in tube distance from the entrance; the tube
  plan a **tree** within `budget.tileCells` (180); landmark joins at most about 40 studs apart
  along a tube; every tube tip closed by a landmark, or its lots never develop.
- **Every building on a tube**, or (axis only) on a lane off a tube.
- **Docking** (new, groundwork rulings): lots, pads and markers stand `dock` (1.75) from a tube's
  centreline along straight and end cells, so nothing bare is left beside a pipe. A landmark's pad
  lies between the tube and the building with its front edge on the dock line, and the building
  stands behind it (about 12.2 from the centreline to the centre of a 9 × 9).
- **Decking arrives with development.** The cluster `blocks` go (a socket, CITY_GROWTH §2.4). Each
  landmark gets one `blocks` rect of its own (one slot per rect) under its pad and building, and
  every fabric prop carries its own deck plate.
- **The skyline rises away from the entrance:** the low early landmarks near it, the Comms Array
  (21.2) and Terraform Station (23.0) toward the back, and the **Launch Tower closing the main
  vista** from the entrance. A candidate that cannot do that says so and shows what closes it.
- **Keep:** the tubes, the monorail loop and its train, the pier off the entrance axis, the
  lattice. Tubes are white half-pipes; only the train moves.
- **Drop from the layout:** `lots`, `plazas`, `treeZones` and the cluster `blocks`. Config
  `lamps: {}` (junction lamps fall inside lots, as on Metropolis); the keys `houses`, `trees`,
  `plazas` and `vehicles` stay because `Scatter` reads them unguarded.
- **Districts** (lead's starting point; the layout owner may move a slot and says why):
  - port: `landingPad`, `roverBay`, `dockingBay`, `spaceportTerminal`, `launchTower`;
  - habitat: `habitatPod`, `hydroponicsDome`, `crewQuarters`, `medicalBay`;
  - industry: `solarArray`, `oxygenGenerator`, `mineralExtractor`, `fusionReactor`,
    `terraformStation`;
  - science: `researchLab`, `commsArray`, `observationDome`;
  - none: `walkwayNetwork` (street-only: a pad on ground nothing else uses, with a one-point
    spur), and the six city-changer candidates below. A low or one-stage slot must not govern lots.
- **City-changer candidates are not decided:** `colonyFlag`, `rockGarden`, `holoBeacon`,
  `lifeSupport`, `orbitalUplink` and `planetaryDefense` keep their models and get ordinary

- **Wild land is raw regolith** (generated `regolith-kit` plus space-kit craters and rocks):

  the plot at tier 0, **including every planned tube cell and the ring band**, and clears as tubes
  draw and lots develop (groundwork rulings). No skirt: the ring is the colony's edge.
- **Lot sizes** (frontage × depth): narrow 4 × 8, small 6 × 6, medium 8 × 12. Two mediums back to
  back fill a pitch-28 block between dock lines exactly (12 + 0.5 + 12 = 24.5). A layout owner who
  needs another size asks the lead with the numbers.
- **Fabric props** grow pod → pod cluster → dome: five stages, `levelStages` [1, 3, 4], stage 0
  at or under `heightFloor` 3.4 (the seeds are the lowest landmarks in the game), final stage at
  most 11 (narrow, small) or 12.5 (medium). The front (−Z) carries an airlock collar flush with
  the lot front. The deck plate covers the lot in the decking colour (96, 98, 108).
- **Targets:** at least **100 lots** at full build (floor 90; `budget.parcels` is 140), building
  sites at every tier, and no tier 4 → full jump above 25 lots. The lot count is written on every
  render.
- **Stand-in models:** this wave's draft props. `plotrender.py` draws blueprints, so nothing is
  uploaded, harvested or templated in this wave.

### Candidates

- **"docks":** a cross tube one cell in from the entrance, with **four avenues** (x = ±14, ±42)
  running from it to the back. Every landmark and every lot docks on a tube; no lanes. A block
  between two avenues holds a landmark and a lot row back to back, or two lot rows. There is no
  tube on the entrance axis, so the owner finds the Launch Tower its strongest seat.
- **"axis":** today's **three avenues** (x = 0, ±28) kept, the centre tube running from the
  entrance to the Launch Tower. Landmarks move up to the dock line, lots fill between and behind
  them, and open **decking lanes** (wave 3.1's tiles-era alleys) carry the back rows where a block
  is deep enough.

### Groundwork rulings (lead, 2026-10-05; mirrored in the tools now, the client follows in wave 4.2)

- **`road.tiles.dock`** (number, optional; Orbital 1.75). In an era that sets it, a planned
  **straight or end** tile cell is a solid only within `dock` of its centreline; lots, pads,
  markers, landmark extents and deck rects may stand in the rest of the cell. Bend, tee and cross
  cells stay whole (a round bend's pipe sweeps its inner corner). Absent means today's rule, the
  whole cell plus pavement, so Metropolis does not move. `fabric.clear.street` is 2.0 for Orbital.
- **Wild on planned tubes.** The rule "wild keeps off every planned street band" holds only in an
  era with `road.tiles.parkStrips`. Without them the wild covers planned cells, laid there as one
  quarter a cell so that a drawn cell clears only itself; a clump never overlaps a planned tube's
  clearing band. `fabric.py check` proves that every wild entry on a planned band is cleared once
  the stretch under it is drawn.
- **`highway.clearBand`** (boolean, optional; Orbital `false`). `false` keeps the ring's band out
  of the clearing mask when `highway.requiresSlot` is owned: the beam is 1.6 wide and the regolith
  stays under it for good. Lots, pads, markers and landmark extents keep off the band as before.
  Wild keeps off the entrance corridor (|x| ≤ 3.5 from the plot's front edge to the first tube
  cell) and is at most 3.0 tall everywhere.
- **Street polylines:** `streetplan.py` allows up to 6 in a tiles era (was 5).
- **`eras.OrbitalColony.fabric`** (config applied by the generator owner from this section):
  `sizes` as above; `heightFloor` 3.4; `levelStages` [1, 3, 4]; `fallbackDistrict` `habitat`;
  `clear` `{ slot 3, pad 1.5, street 2.0, parcel 1.5, lane 2.0 }`; `lanes`
  `{ width 3, rim 0, fillHeight 0.09 }`; `reveal` `RevealScaffold`; `marker` prop `LotBeacon`,
  offset [5.3, 0, −0.5]; `padLook` Metal (170, 174, 184); `construction` as Metropolis; `pull`
  Metropolis's values as first values for the layout owners to tune. Draft props:

  | District | narrow | small | medium |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | habitat | `FabricHabNarrowA`, `FabricHabNarrowB` | `FabricHabSmallA` | `FabricHabMediumA` |
  | industry | `FabricIndNarrowA` | `FabricIndSmallA` | `FabricIndMediumA` |
  | science | `FabricSciNarrowA` | `FabricSciSmallA` | `FabricHabMediumA` |
  | port | `FabricPortNarrowA` | `FabricPortSmallA` | `FabricPortMediumA` |

  `sites` `SiteNarrow`, `SiteSmall`, `SiteMedium`; `siteVariants` narrow
  `[SiteNarrow, SiteNarrowGantry, SiteNarrow]`, small `[SiteSmall, SiteSmallGantry]`; `wild.clumps`
  `RegolithClumpA/B/C` (13 × 13), `wild.quarters` `RegolithQuarterA/B/C` (6.5 × 6.5, in the local
  +X, +Z quadrant like the old-town quarters), `quarterRadius` 3.3, `singleRadius` 1.0; plan
  singles `RegolithBoulder` [2, 2], `RegolithCrater` [3, 3], `SurveyBeacon` [1, 1].
- **Not in this wave:** `Types.luau`, `CityFabric.luau`, the client and `check_mirror.py`'s era
  list. Orbital joins the cross-check in wave 4.2, when the client copies these rules.

### Rulings after the groundwork (lead, 2026-10-05)

The generator, the mirror and the renderer run Orbital end to end (`m12o_groundwork_full.png`: today's
tubes, 13 lots, 54 clumps, 23 deck rects), with every gate green and the three shipped eras' fabric
data byte-identical. 28 draft blueprints exist (`colony-kit`, `regolith-kit`).

- **Wild on planned tubes, as built:** the data has no lone quarter (an entry is a whole clump or a
  single), so the wild is laid as **lattice-aligned clumps**: each quarter of a clump is one 7-stud
  cell, a clump may straddle a planned tube, and a drawn cell clears only the quarter on it. The
  sentence "a clump never overlaps a planned tube's clearing band" above is withdrawn. `fabric.py
  check` holds the intent with three rules: a wild entry on a planned band is cleared by the stretch
  under it; one quarter a cell; a drawn stretch clears nothing off its own cells.
- **A clump is its quarter at four turns** (the client breaks a clump into its quarters), so the
  four-fold repeat in the regolith clumps stays for the mock. A mixed mapping (`wild.clumpQuarters`)
  is a wave 4.2 option if the repeat shows on the plot renders.
- **Cells the clump grid cannot cover carry singles.** The plot is 17 cells across and a clump is
  two, so one ring column and one ring row, and the cells beside the entrance corridor, get no
  clump. Each such cell gets one single (boulder, crater or beacon by the seeded pattern), at least
  1.5 from a pier foot's centre, inside `budget.wild`. No ring side is bare.
- **Lots keep off deck rects.** No lot overlaps a landmark's `blocks` rect (flush is allowed); the
  generator treats the rects as solids and `check` proves it. A landmark's deck stays one rect.
- **Docked measurements, confirmed:** a footprint, harvested extents, a pad, a marker and a deck rect
  are judged against the dock line (1.75) on straight and end cells and against the whole cell on
  bend, tee and cross cells. A lane's slab reaches 1.5 from the centreline, as a spur footpath does,
  and is judged against the 3-wide walkway and whole cells.
- **Piers under the beam:** clumps are low relief and may stand around a pier foot; only singles keep
  off it.
- **Marker colours:** `stakeColor` (255, 160, 52), `stringColor` (214, 216, 222).
- **Draft props, accepted for the mock** with these notes for the final set: `LotBeacon` is small
  and close to the sites' work light; `FabricHabNarrowB` reads as an office block at stage 4;
  `FabricHabSmallA` and `FabricHabMediumA` share one motif; `FabricSciSmallA` echoes the Comms
  Array; the medium industry and port decks are half empty at stages 0 and 1. Fabric blueprints use
  scale 2.0 so the space-kit cargo craft fit a lot. Masts and flare stacks count toward a prop's
  height, so a low governor holds those props a stage back; kept for the mock.
- **A tube walled by tall rows disappears from the tycoon camera** (rows of 7 to 10 studs over a
  1.9-stud pipe, 3.5 apart). The layout owners report how much of the tube network shows at full
  build; a low front step on every fabric prop is the lever in reserve.
- **For the client in wave 4.2:** `Fabric.buildMask` skips the ring rects when
  `highway.clearBand == false`; types for `road.tiles.dock` and `highway.clearBand`; Orbital joins
  `check_mirror.py`. Docking is a tools rule and needs no client code.

### Rulings after the first layouts (lead, 2026-10-05)

- **Lots against a landmark's path:** in a docked era a tube lot keeps `parcels.spur` off the **laid**
  footpath, not off the path's end on the centreline. A join no longer costs the far-side row 3.6
  studs (axis measured 92 → 99 in a scratch run). Other eras do not move.
- **`parcels.lanes.lines[].front`** (`"left"` | `"right"`, optional): fixes which side a lane's row
  answers to; absent means the nearest lot, as before.
- **Wild in the ring band is cleared by nothing** when `highway.clearBand` is false. A developed
  outer row cleared the band's quarters (lot back at 52, quarter centre at 56, reach 4.8), and
  `clear.parcel` cannot drop under 1.3 (`check`: margin + `quarterRadius` must cover a quarter's
  half-diagonal, 4.60). `check` also refuses a street cell or a deck rect in the band.
- **Sizes are mixed:** each candidate seats at least 12 small or medium lots, at least 4 medium, so
  the glass domes appear. The mix costs one lot on either candidate.
- **Second narrow props** `FabricIndNarrowB`, `FabricSciNarrowB`, `FabricPortNarrowB` (config
  applied): a row of one district alternates two buildings.
- **Growth is even:** both sides of the colony are growing by tier 3.

### Ben at the gate (2026-10-05): both candidates rejected

"i dont really love it, i was looking for something more organic looking for the orbital colony, it
looks way to similar to metropolly". A comb of straight avenues lined with terrace rows inside a
square ring is Metropolis's plan in white, whichever candidate is picked; the lead framed both that
way. `m12-orbital-docks` and `m12-orbital-axis` stay as the record and are not built on.

Asked what organic should mean, Ben chose:
- **Curving tubes** (over hubs and spokes, and over clusters on today's square pieces): tubes bend
  and wander like Village's trails and Boomtown's streets, and pods turn to follow them. He was told
  it needs new tube meshes and one harvest paste later.
- **As dense as organic allows** (over clusters with open regolith between them).
- **A round monorail loop** (over the square ring).

## Wave 4.1b — organic Orbital (a second mock gate for Ben, not yet a contract)

Two new candidate layouts, again real layouts through the real generator. Everything in wave 4.1
holds unless this section changes it: the frozen slots, the growth rules of mock B, districts, the
lot sizes (4 × 8, 6 × 6, 8 × 12), five-stage props with `levelStages` [1, 3, 4] and `heightFloor`
3.4, decking that arrives with development, lots off a landmark's decking, the regolith as wild,
the draft props, and "nothing uploaded in this wave".

### What changes

- **Orbital leaves the tiles family.** Its tubes are curving streets like Village's and Boomtown's:
  polylines in the layout, smoothed by the arcs those eras use, cut into the same pieces
  (`tools/paths/network.py`), and each piece **swept as a half-pipe mesh** in today's profile
  (radius 1.5 on a 0.3 sill, 3.24 wide, a grey ring every 1.4). In wave 4.2 the meshes go the
  baked-paths route (one upload per layout, one harvest paste). A centreline never curves tighter
  than a 6-stud radius.
- **A hub at every node.** `TubeHub`, a round airlock hub wider than the pipe, stands where tubes
  branch and where one ends. A swept piece runs from hub to hub and ends inside both, so two tube
  meshes never meet in the open.
- **Landmark connections and back lanes are flat decking**, never tubes (a buy pad must stay in
  view): baked flat pieces in today's spur look, Metal (170, 174, 184), 3 wide. A landmark's piece
  is its **apron**: the footpath from the tube widened under its pad and building. It replaces wave
  4.1's `blocks` rect, which only a tiles era draws.
- **Lots follow the tubes:** fronts 1.75 from the centreline (the pipe's half-width is 1.62), each
  lot turned to the tube's tangent; narrow lots may terrace along a curve. The docking rule
  (`road.tiles.dock`), the laid-footpath rule for docked eras and the 6-polyline allowance are
  withdrawn with the tiles: no era uses them, so their code goes.
- **Round monorail:** `highway.round` (boolean, loop mode only). The track is a circle of radius
  `ring` (56) about the plot's centre, in 48 segments of 7.5° (`MonorailArc`, beam 1.6 wide, top
  7.07, soffit 6.10), segment joints on multiples of 7.5° from +X, one pier at each segment's middle
  (so the entrance axis falls between two piers). The band is the annulus 52.5 to 59.5 from the
  centre: no lot, pad, marker, apron or landmark extents in it, nothing taller than 3.0 under it.
  **The colony may spill past the loop** into the plot's corners: a tube may cross the band, at 60°
  or more to the track and 2 or more from a pier foot. The train follows the circle.
- **Wild is an irregular scatter**, never a visible grid: clumps, quarters and singles placed and
  turned by the seeded pattern Village's woods use (or the fields pattern at an angle with jitter,
  whichever reads as ground). It stays under the beam for good (`highway.clearBand` false, now the
  annulus) and in every pocket the lots leave.
- **Fabric props are round:** capsules, drums, spheres, domes and vaults. No box body with storey
  bands of windows: those read as Metropolis's towers. Deck plates and airlock collars stay.
- **Targets:** as dense as organic allows. At least **90 lots** at full build (floor 80; Village
  holds 116, Boomtown 75), building sites at every tier, no tier 4 → full jump above 25 lots, the
  lot count on every render.

### Candidates

- **"vine":** one main tube winds from the entrance to the Launch Tower in a long S, and side tubes

### Rulings after the organic groundwork (lead, 2026-10-05)

The tools run Orbital as a path era end to end (`m12o_groundwork_organic_full.png`: four curving
polylines, 232 studs of tube in 28 swept pieces, 8 hubs, 23 aprons, one lane, the round loop with
its train, 14 lots), every gate green and the three shipped eras' fabric data byte-identical.

- **Butt joints.** A tube is one mesh per stretch with the ids the baked paths use (`L…`), so it
  grows with the buildings and the client clones it by id. Stretches end at every landmark join and
  bend; where no hub stands, two pieces butt on one cross-section, and a closed disc caps a tube
  that has not grown on. A hub stands only where a tube ends, branches, or two chains meet. The
  sentence "two tube meshes never meet in the open" above is withdrawn.
- **Two tubes into one hub leave it 90° or more apart** (closer, the pipes meet outside the 4.6-wide
  hub). `tubes.py` checks it; a corner is rounded at radius 6.48 and a bend under radius 6 is
  refused.
- **Config as built:** `road.width` 3.24; `road.paths.spurWidth` 3, `road.paths.tube
  { hub = "TubeHub", front = 1.75 }`, `road.paths.deck { material, color }`; `road.tiles` is gone
  from Orbital; `highway.round` true, `highway.clearBand` false, `highway.props.arc`
  `MonorailArc`; `fabric.clear.street` 3.5. Plan: `parcels.frontSetback` 1.75,
  `parcels.lanes.lines[].front`, `wild.clumps.inset`, `wild.singles.between`.
- **Aprons are automatic:** a landmark's path, pad rect and building rect, each grown 0.25, as one
  flat decking mesh (`SP_<slotId>`). Lots keep off aprons, so apron-free frontage is the density
  budget (the 23 landmarks take about 275 studs).
- **The band:** only a tube crosses it, at 60° or more to the track and 2.0 from a pier foot measured
  from the tube's centreline (feet at 3.75° + 7.5°·k). Everything else keeps 0.5 clear. Wild under
  the beam is cleared by nothing (`ring_keeps`, on the annulus); a round loop has no ring rects.
- **Street polylines stay at most 5**; a candidate that needs a sixth asks with numbers.
- **Wild plates never overlap** (two clump plates over each other are coplanar faces and flicker in
  game, as Boomtown's first lanes did), and **an entrance apron** runs from the plot's front edge
  (0, −60) to the entrance hub between two piers. Both are being added to the generator.
- **Props, as revised:** the fifteen fabric props are built from round forms and are lower (habitat
  narrow tops out near 6.1, science near 7.9, industry near 10.4). `TubeHub` 4.6 × 4.6 × 2.6, no
  facing. `MonorailArc` 7.44 × 1.92 × 7.12, origin at the segment's middle on the circle; a segment
  whose middle is at angle t from +X sits at (56 cos t, 0, 56 sin t) with rotationY −(t + 90)°.
  `LotBeacon` is 4.5 tall.
- **For the client in wave 4.2** (replaces the wave 4.1 list): Orbital moves from `TileRenderer` to
  the path renderer (a tube per `L…` id, decking per `SP_…` and `LN_…`, one mesh and no rim); a
  `TubeHub` at each hub node once a tube there is drawn; the round loop (48 `MonorailArc`, the train
  on the circle, no ramp); `CityFabric.luau` copies `ring_keeps` and "no ring rects on a round
  loop"; the asset run uploads the swept and flat pieces (52 on the groundwork) through the palette
  route, with one harvest paste and a `bake.py --list` gate for Orbital.

selene, `check_compile.py`, a Rojo build). Sheet: `assets/testfit/out/OrbitalColony/
m12o_compare_organic.png`.

What the two layouts proved:
- **Dense and wandering pull against each other on this plot.** The ground within 10 studs of the
  round loop is a third of the colony, and only a tube that follows the loop about 41 studs out can
  front it. Vine's drafts that wandered to the corners instead held 48 to 58 lots. Every radian a
  tube turns costs about 8 studs of its inside row.
- **Mediums cost lots on curves** (Bloom 95 all narrow, 82 with the mix; Vine 69 without mediums),
  and **lanes barely work**: pockets between curving tubes are under 15 wide.
- A landmark inside a ring blanks 16 to 20 studs of frontage (pad, marker, pinch).

Asks held for after Ben's answer (not built): `STREET_COUNT` 5 → 7 and `budget.roadPieces`
60 → 68 or 76 (two more curls, about 8 lots each by the vine owner's estimate; 15° corners on
Bloom's outer ring); the marker offset mirrored per slot (about 6 lots on Bloom); a per-stretch
size list in `fabric.py` (mediums without the inner-row loss). Rulings taken as built: the Launch
Tower and the Solar Array carry no district on Vine; the Comms Array is the spire of Bloom's heart,
not at the back; the monorail pad stands outside the loop on Vine.

## Wave 4.1c — city-changers on Bloom (step 3; renders for Ben, not yet a contract)

Orbital's `walkwayNetwork` is already a street upgrade (the monorail). Six more slots could "stop
being a sole building": a slot that does becomes `streetOnly` and drives an upgrade layer or a prop
swap. Each proposal is shown to Ben as a before and after render; the economy is untouched either
way (type, cost, income, multiplier and `requires` stay).

| Slot | Proposal | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `colonyFlag` (8) | **Raise the Colony Flags**: flag masts along the tubes | the generic upgrade layer (`ColonyFlagMast` beside the tubes, between lots) |
| `lifeSupport` (12) | **Green the Domes**: every habitat pod and dome gets a garden under its glass | a prop swap (`fabric.swaps`, suffix `Green`) to twins of the four habitat props |
| `rockGarden` (14) | **Tend the Rock Gardens**: raked rock-and-crystal gardens fill the strips between rows and beside aprons | the generic upgrade layer (`RockGardenA`, `RockGardenB` in the gaps the lots leave) |
| `holoBeacon` (20) | **Light the Holo Beacons**: a hologram over every tube hub | the generic upgrade layer, placed at the hubs (`HubBeacon`) |
| `orbitalUplink` (17), `planetaryDefense` (23) | stay buildings (lead's recommendation): the corners past the loop want landmarks, and the last purchases read better as buildings | none |

- **Layout:** the four slots keep their order and economy and become street-only on the branch for
  the mock (a pad on ground nothing else uses, with a one-point spur). The Bloom owner reseats so no
  tube tip is left without a landmark and uses the freed seats; the lot count is reported before and
  after, per changer and for all four.
- **Rock gardens answer Bloom's weak point:** 36% of the ground inside the loop is uncovered, as
  1.5 to 4-stud strips. A garden is low (at most 1.2), keeps 0.25 off lots, aprons and tubes, and is a
  mesh at least 0.05 above the plot.
- **Twins share the body** and change only what is under the glass, so the swap plays as a stage
  swap. A twin exists for every stage of its original.
- **Budgets:** flags at most 24, gardens at most 40, beacons one per hub (11).

## Wave 4.2 — Orbital in the game (Ben, 2026-10-06)

The mock becomes the game. The layout, the plan, the fabric data, the config and the Python tools
are done and green; this wave makes the game draw what the mirror draws, finishes the props, and
prepares the asset run. Nothing is uploaded until Ben approves the final prop sheets.

### Slots (lead, `Config/Eras/4_OrbitalColony.json`, applied)

`colonyFlag` "Raise the Colony Flags", `lifeSupport` "Green the Domes", `rockGarden` "Tend the Rock
Gardens" and `holoBeacon` "Light the Holo Beacons" are `streetOnly`, as `walkwayNetwork` "Build the
Monorail" already is. Order, type, cost, income, multiplier and `requires` are untouched
(`sim_economy.py`: 16:20:04, legacy 887).

### What the game must draw (the mirror is normative: `tools/cityfabric.py`, `tools/paths/tubes.py`, `tools/fabric.py`, `tools/testfit/plotrender.py`)

- **Orbital is a path era.** `eras.OrbitalColony.road` has no `tiles`; it has `width` 3.24,
  `paths.spurWidth` 3, `paths.tube { hub = "TubeHub", front = 1.75 }` and `paths.deck { material,
  color }`. The client lays it with the baked-path renderer, not `TileRenderer`:
  - a **tube** per street piece id (`L…`, the ids `tools/paths/network.py` yields): one swept
    half-pipe mesh, no rim, growing with the buildings as Village's and Boomtown's paths do;
  - **decking** per `SP_<slotId>` (a landmark's apron: its path, pad and building rects as one flat
    mesh), per `LN_…` (none on Bloom) and `SP_entrance` (laid from the start, tied to no slot);
  - a **`TubeHub`** at every hub node (where a tube ends, branches, or two chains meet) once a tube
    at that node is drawn. The hub rule is `tubes.py`'s; copy it, do not re-derive it.
  - Before the asset run there are no templates: every piece degrades to a placeholder Part or to
    nothing, never to an error.
- **Round monorail.** `highway.round` true (loop mode, no ramp): 48 `highway.props.arc`
  (`MonorailArc`) seats on the circle of radius `layout.highway.ring` (56); the seat whose middle is
  at angle t = 3.75° + 7.5°·k from +X stands at (56 cos t, 0, 56 sin t) with rotationY −(t + 90)°;
  the train rides the circle at `deckHeight`; the reveal runs round the loop from the entrance.
- **Pure rules, in `src/shared/CityFabric.luau`** (so `check_mirror.py --strict` covers them; Orbital
  joins its era list): `ring_keeps` (with `highway.clearBand == false` a wild quarter or single whose
  point lies on the ring band is cleared by nothing), no ring rects on a round loop, `fabric.wildSwaps`
  (each standing clump, quarter and single shows `<prop><suffix>` for every owned swap, in list
  order, where that template exists), and an upgrade item with `anchor = "highway"` (valid without
  `stretch` or `parcel`; developed while the highway stands).
- **Client `Fabric.luau`:** `syncWild` applies the wild swaps and re-syncs when the slot is bought;
  the `flags` layer's pier banners use the highway anchor; the ring rules come from `CityFabric`.
  The file stands at 170 of 180 top-level locals: fold its constants into tables and move its
  validation block to its own module **before** adding anything (`py tools/check_compile.py` is the
  gate).
- **Nothing else moves:** the server, remotes, the economy, the other eras' config, layouts and
  fabric data (byte-identical), and Metropolis's tile renderer.

### Rulings after the wave 4.2 reports (lead, 2026-10-06)

- **Shared API (`CityFabric.luau`):** `RoundLoop(highway, layoutHighway)` (round means
  `round == true` and no layout ramp), `RingBand(highway, layoutHighway): FabricBand?` (the band is
  `ring` ± `highway.bandHalf`; bad or absent config means no band), `KeptInBand(px, pz, band)`,
  `RingGround(highway, layoutHighway, tileStuds, ramp, rampCells)` (empty without `requiresSlot`, with
  `clearBand == false`, or on a round loop), `ValidWildSwaps`, `SwappedWild(prop, swaps, owned,
  exists)`, `ValidUpgradeItem`, `HighwayBuilt`, `UpgradeDeveloped(item, stretches, states,
  highwayBuilt)`. Which wild placements stand, their base names and `exists` stay the client's.
- **Client:** `Tubes.luau` (pure: the hub rule and the entrance apron, copied from `tubes.py`) and
  `FabricValidation.luau` are new; `Fabric.luau` went from 170 to 130 top-level locals. A template
  for piece id `L…` or `SP_…` lives at `ReplicatedStorage.Assets.Paths.OrbitalColony.<pieceId>`: a
  Model with an identity pivot and one MeshPart `Fill`, no `Rim`; the client clones it and never
  turns it. Hubs spend no budget and show on far plots; `SP_entrance` is always shown and is not
  counted against `pathPieces` in the client; a missing hub, arc or prop draws nothing, with one
  warning per era and kind; no train runs until an arc stands.

### Review rulings (2026-10-06, wave 4.2 review at 87de142: 0 Critical, 1 Major, 4 Minor)

- **Major, fixed (0f526ae):** regolith kept under the monorail reached into lots. `KeptInBand` keeps a
  quarter by its quad point, but a quarter is a quadrant of a round feature anchored at the clump's
  centre and reaches up to 4.6 studs past that point. Five cases on the shipped data (a mound in a
  science pod, a boulder ring in two pods, one more lot, the Rover Bay's pad and apron). The
  generator and `check` now keep a band-kept quarter's or single's ground off every lot, pad, apron

## Rulings (Ben, 2026-10-12)

1. **Variants: free styles in the Armory.** Every owned family offers all its variants; switching
   happens only in the lobby and between waves. (Wave 2. Wave 1 plays the range's loadout.)
2. **One 10-wave skeleton for every era,** scaled per era by config: fodder in waves 1–2, the
   slinger in 3, the brute in 4, the **Colossus** as the boss of wave 5, marksman and lobber in
   6–7, plated elites in 8–9, the **Warlord and his guard** as the boss of wave 10.
3. **Going down: a teammate standing near revives you,** with no button. Solo, the first down
   ends the run. (The revive is Wave 4. Wave 1 ships the solo rule and the seam: one
   `WaveService.OnDown` rule function and a `PartyMember.down` field.)
4. **`proving.rbxl` boots into a mission.** The range stays as a Studio-only bench behind a
   config switch.

## Wave 1 — crowd in a mission (Village, solo)

**Goal.** Play opens on Raider Woods, wave 1, fought with the range's weapons against crowd
enemies. All ten waves run, with the Colossus at wave 5 and the Warlord at wave 10. Rewards are
paid per kind into the existing pool, split and flush. Health and damage follow the player's
Armory tiers. Solo, the first down ends the run. Every number is config.

### What the study got right, and what the code corrected (lead, checked 2026-10-12)

- **Right:** the crowd modules (`CrowdService`, `CrowdBrain`, `ThreatField`, `CrowdCodec`,
  `HitShapes`) are place-agnostic. The gates are `RangeService.Configure`, `RangeService.IsActive`
  (read by `AbilityService.Start`/`AddPlayer`/`OnCast`) and `CameraController.IsRange()` (eight
  client modules). `VitalsService.Start` is called only by `RangeService.Start`.
- **Corrected: there is one strike choke point, not two.** `RangeService.Strike` (the ability
  hook) resolves through the same local `strike()` as every weapon hit, projectile, chain jump and
  the slam. `strike()` is the only caller of `CrowdService.Damage`.
- **Corrected: `CombatService` is more than hits.** It also batches the mission effects
  (`PushFx`: `wave`, `bossDown`, `mentor`, `kill`), keeps the damage tally that the contribution
  split reads, and is `ArenaService`'s share source (`SetShareSource`). Unmounting it moves those
  to `RunFx` (new) and `WaveService`.
- **Corrected: `EnemyService` cannot simply leave the tree.** `ArenaService` requires it for the
  arena geometry setters, the collision group and the bot rig builder, and `DebugService` for the
  bots. In Wave 1 both modules stay in the tree and are required, but **never Init'd or Started**,
  and nothing in the mission path calls their run functions.
- **Corrected: two writers of MaxHealth.** `ArenaService.applyMaxHp` writes the profile's
  `Armory.MaxHp`, and `VitalsService.PrepareCharacter` pins tier 1 (range ruling 17). In
  missions `VitalsService` becomes the only writer of a human's MaxHealth.
- **Corrected: scales need an API.** `CrowdService.Spawn` reads HP and plate from the kind def
  only. A boss's summons are raised inside `CrowdService` (`summon()`), not by `WaveService`. So
  the mission scales must be crowd-wide, set once per run (`SetScales`), and not passed per spawn.
- **Corrected: armour is a flat tier-1 number too** (`max(amount - armor, amount * armorFloor)`).
  It is judged on the unscaled amount like `heavyHit` and plates, or it would fade with tier.
- **Corrected: "recommended power" is gear 2/1, not tier 1.** In `docs/BALANCE.md`, Raider Woods
  is "60 (2/1, 57)": melee tier 2 and ranged tier 1 give power 57. The reward band comes from the
  same line: 142,185 cash, 256 Timber, 35 Valor, 8:32.
- **Corrected: a run's end kicks in Studio.** The summary's group return uses the Studio bridge,
  which kicks the player. A proving mission therefore restarts in place instead (ruling 19).

**Known limits carried into Wave 1 (told to Ben, not fixed):**
- The crowd walks through the arena's boulders and fence posts, as in the range.
- The keepAway bands (marksman 28–45) were tuned in a 220-stud arena. In 110 they span most of the
  floor, and the brain stops at the bound.

### Boot sequence (`src/combat/server/Main.server.luau`)

```
mode = CombatMode.Get()                         -- once, before anything
RemoteService.Configure(CombatRemotes)
WeaponService.Configure(mode)                   -- active in both modes when Tuning is available
RangeService.Configure(mode == "range")
ArenaService.SetSnapshotSender(sendSnapshot)
ordered Init, then Start:
  DataService, RemoteService, RunRegistry,
  ArenaService,
  WeaponService     -- Start: VitalsService.Start(i-frame hooks); its Heartbeat (projectiles, air, i-frames)
  RangeService      -- range only: proving arena, CrowdService.SetBounds, WeaponService.SetArena, default set
  AbilityService    -- both modes (gate: WeaponService.IsActive())
  waveBoot          -- WaveService.Init (mission hooks; inert in the range) + Boot (its loop)
  DebugService
  returnBoot
```

- **No `EnemyService` and no `CombatService` in the list.** Main no longer requires them.
- **`runJoinSequence`, range:** `RangeService.AddPlayer` (which calls `WeaponService.AddPlayer`),
  `AbilityService.AddPlayer`, snapshot. Unchanged otherwise.
- **`runJoinSequence`, mission:** as today up to `ArenaService.Admit`, then
  `WeaponService.AddPlayer(player)`, `AbilityService.AddPlayer(player)`, snapshot. A mission with
  `crowd == nil` is refused before `EnsureRun` (ruling 27).
- **Character:** in missions, `ArenaService`'s CharacterAdded handler ends with the character hook
  (`ArenaService.SetCharacterHook`). `WaveService.Init` points that hook at
  `WeaponService.PrepareCharacter`, which resets the shooter's air state and calls
  `VitalsService.PrepareCharacter`. In the range, `RangeService` places the body and then calls
  `WeaponService.PrepareCharacter`.
- **`releasePlayer`:** `AbilityService.RemovePlayer`, `RangeService.RemovePlayer` (range),
  `WeaponService.RemovePlayer`, then `ArenaService.Remove` etc. as today.
- **Handlers:** `RequestRangeAttack` → `WeaponService.OnAttack`, `RequestRangeDraw` →
  `WeaponService.OnDraw`, `RequestDash` → `WeaponService.OnDash`, `RequestSlam` →
  `WeaponService.OnSlam`, `RequestRangeAbility` → `AbilityService.OnCast`, `RequestTune` /
  `RequestRangeCommand` → `RangeService` (inert outside the range). `RequestReady`: ignored when
  `RangeService.IsActive()` and also in a proving mission (ruling 19). The four old handlers are
  removed.
- **Run start (`WaveService.Start`):** reads `Combat.CrowdWave(mission, startWave, …)` and calls
  `CrowdService.SetScales({ hp = spec.hpScale, plate = spec.plateScale })`,
  `VitalsService.SetMission(rules)` (ruling 11, with `damageScale` and `regenShare` from the spec),
  `WeaponService.SetArena(ArenaService.ArenaBounds())` and `CrowdService.SetBounds(...)` (the
  first run only; the arena is built at the world origin like every arena). Every member then
  stands up at full health.
  - **Corrected 2026-10-13 (second review):** the bounds are set whenever
    `ArenaService.ArenaName()` differs from the arena they were last set for, not only on the
    first run (a reserved server may host a second run in another arena).
  - **Added 2026-10-13:** `Start` does nothing until `VitalsService.AllHaveBodies(members)` is
    true. The lobby polls it again next frame.
- **Rejoin (added 2026-10-13):** in `runJoinSequence`, a player who is still down from an
  earlier run is stood up (`VitalsService.StandUp`) just before `ArenaService.Admit`, so the
  first RunState already says so. The "range was asked for but could not boot" early return
  is removed: it could not be reached.
- **Boot print:** `[Combat] booted — mission (crowd)`, `— mission (crowd, proving: <missionId> from wave <n>)`
  or `— Proving Grounds (range)`.

### `CombatMode` and the proving switch

- `src/shared/CombatMode.luau` (new; uses `RunService`, `Workspace`, `Catalog`, `Tuning`; not
  pure, and it must not be required by `CrowdService` or `VitalsService`, which the harness
  loads):
  - `CombatMode.Get(): Types.CombatMode`, cached after the first call. On a client it first
    waits for `game.Loaded` in Studio, exactly as `CameraController.detectRange` does today.
  - `CombatMode.IsProving(): boolean` = Studio and `Workspace[debug.provingAttribute] == true`.
    **Corrected 2026-10-13 (second review):** it is no longer read live. One `decide()` reads
    proving and range together, once, behind `game.Loaded` on a Studio client, and caches
    both. `IsProving()` therefore yields like `Get()`.
- `tools/proving_project.py` keeps baking `DebugProving = true`, and also bakes
  `DebugMission = debug.provingMission` (the existing `missionAttribute`, which also bypasses the
  era lock in Studio).
- **The switches, all in `Combat.json debug`, flipped by the lead and followed by "Build all":**
  - `provingBoots`: `"mission"` (P5 default) or `"range"` (the bench, every P1–P4 set as before).
  - `provingMission`: `"village"`.
  - `provingStartWave`: `1`. Set it to 5 or 10 for a boss-only build.
  - `provingStartDelay`: `3` seconds.
  - `provingGear`: `{ "melee": 2, "ranged": 1 }`. Optional `ascension` `{ melee, ranged }`.
- **In play (Studio only, mission mode):** **B** skips to the next boss wave (5, then 10), and
  **N** skips to the next wave. Both go through `RequestDebug("skip", "boss" | "next")`. A small
  Studio-only hint in the HUD corner reads `B boss · N next wave`.

### Server modules (luau-engineer; run as two instances A and B with the disjoint files below)

**A — weapons.**

- **`WeaponService.luau` (new)**, moved from `RangeService` with the behaviour unchanged except
  rulings 7, 8 and 21. It must stay at ≤ 180 top-level locals; group constants and state into
  tables from the start. Public API:
  ```luau
  WeaponService.Configure(mode: Types.CombatMode): ()
  WeaponService.IsActive(): boolean
  WeaponService.Mode(): Types.CombatMode
  WeaponService.Init(): ()
  WeaponService.Start(): ()            -- VitalsService.Start({ iframeWindow, grantIframes }); Heartbeat
  WeaponService.SetArena(center: Vector3, halfSize: Vector3): ()
  WeaponService.SetActGate(gate: ((player: Player) -> boolean)?): ()   -- ruling 21; nil = always
  WeaponService.SetStatsProvider(provider: ((player: Player, stats: Types.RangeStats) -> ())?): ()
  WeaponService.AddPlayer(player: Player): ()        -- loadout = ProvingGrounds.json loadout (Wave 1)
  WeaponService.RemovePlayer(player: Player): ()
  WeaponService.PrepareCharacter(player: Player, character: Model): ()
  WeaponService.GearOf(player: Player): (Types.SlotTiers, Types.SlotTiers)  -- (gear, ascension), ruling 12
  WeaponService.DamageScale(player: Player, slot: string, ability: boolean): number  -- 1 in the range
  WeaponService.AbandonProjectiles(): ()
  WeaponService.OnAttack / OnDraw / OnDash / OnSlam   -- signatures as RangeService's today
  WeaponService.IsInvulnerable / IframeWindow / GrantIframes
  -- AbilityService hooks, signatures unchanged from RangeService:
  WeaponService.LoadoutOf / RootOf / CheckAim / GroundPoint / FloorBelow / SeedFor
  WeaponService.Strike / FireProjectile / SetAttackBuff / SetAbilityLock / OnLoadoutChanged
  ```
  - `GearOf` in the range returns tier 1 in both slots and ascension 0. In a proving mission it
    returns `debug.provingGear` when present. Otherwise it returns the profile's
    `combat.gear` and `combat.ascension`.
  - `RangeStats` is assembled here (refusals, `lastHits`, `lastKills`, `dps`, ability totals). The
    provider (set by `RangeService`) fills `clearSeconds`, `alive`, `serverFrameMs`,
    `damageTaken`, `downs` and `god`. In missions it is still sent, because the client needs
    `refusedSeq`.
  - `TuneState` (overrides + loadout) is sent at `AddPlayer` in both modes. Overrides are always
    empty in missions.
- **`RangeService.luau`**: keeps `Configure`, `IsActive`, `AddPlayer`/`RemovePlayer` (wrapping
  `WeaponService`), `Start`, the sets, respawns, `OnTune`, `OnCommand` and the stats provider. Its
  header documents what moved. The behaviour in the range is byte-for-byte that of P4.
- **`AbilityService.luau`**: requires `WeaponService` instead of `RangeService`. Its gate is
  `WeaponService.IsActive()`. `OnCast` also honours the act gate. Kill refunds use the unchanged
  `(id, byUserId)` of `OnKilled`.
- **`StrikeTally.luau`**: `StrikeTally.New(scale: number?)`, and `Tally.scale` (default 1) is
  what `strike()` passes to `CrowdService.Damage`.
- **`src/shared/Armory.luau`**: adds the pure `Armory.DamageScale(cfg, slot, tier, ascLevel,
  ability): number`. It is 1 when the tier-1 damage is 0 or the slot is unknown, and it is mirrored
  in `tools/sim_range.py` and `tools/sim_combat.py`. **Corrected 2026-10-13 (second review):**
  it is also 1 for a tier whose own damage is 0, so a hit never staggers and removes no HP.

**B — the mission.**

- **`CrowdService.luau`**:
  ```luau
  export type CrowdScales = { hp: number, plate: number }
  export type CrowdKillInfo = {
  	id: number, kind: string, boss: boolean, position: Vector3,
  	byUserId: number, damageBy: { [number]: number },
  }
  CrowdService.SetScales(scales: CrowdScales): ()        -- default { hp = 1, plate = 1 }; the range never calls it
  CrowdService.Spawn(kind, position, behaviour, anchor: Vector3?, hpMult: number?): number
  	-- maxHp = max(def.hp * scales.hp * (hpMult or 1), 1); plate = (def.plate or 0) * scales.plate
  	-- summon() spawns take scales.hp and no hpMult
  CrowdService.Damage(id, amount, byUserId, push?, launch?, scale: number?): (number, boolean, Verdict?)
  	-- ruling 9; scale nil = 1; the guarded test is unchanged
  CrowdService.OnKilled(callback: (id: number, byUserId: number, info: CrowdKillInfo) -> ()): ()
  CrowdService.KillAll(byUserId: number): number         -- every living body dies through the death path
  ```
  - `damageBy` lives on the record and is built in `Damage`.
  - Perf line: ruling 26. Use a fixed ring of step times, no allocation per step, and sort a copy
    only when printing.
  - In the range, every value with `scale = 1` and `scales = {1, 1}` is identical to P4. The
    harness proves it.
- **`VitalsService.luau`**:
  ```luau
  export type MissionRules = {
  	mayJudge: (player: Player) -> boolean,   -- ruling 13: targeting AND judging
  	onDown: (player: Player) -> (),          -- ruling 18; called once per down, after the frame's batch
  	maxHpOf: (player: Player) -> number?,    -- Armory.MaxHp(GearOf); nil = leave the Humanoid's
  	damageScale: number,
  	regenShare: number,
  }
  VitalsService.SetMission(rules: MissionRules?): ()   -- nil = range rules (P4, unchanged)
  VitalsService.SetGod(player: Player, on: boolean): ()
  VitalsService.StandUp(player: Player): ()            -- ends a down, full health, getUpIframes
  VitalsService.RefreshMaxHp(player: Player): ()       -- keeps the health share
  VitalsService.ClearThreats(): ()                     -- OnSetLoaded's clearing half; OnSetLoaded calls it
  ```
  - In mission mode:
    - The damage of a landed hit is `math.max(math.round(attack.damage * damageScale), 1)` for any
      `attack.damage > 0`. This happens at the one place an attack's damage is read, the queue and
      travelling contacts alike.
    - Regen is `regenShare * MaxHealth` per second after `player.regenDelay`.
    - A down never ends by itself.
    - `PrepareCharacter` writes MaxHealth from `maxHpOf` and fills the health.
    - The `canTarget` threat hook is `not down and mayJudge(player)`.
  - The module still requires no `ArenaService`, `WaveService` or `CombatMode`: it learns all of
    it through `SetMission`.
- **`WaveService.luau`**: requires `CrowdService`, `VitalsService`, `WeaponService` and `RunFx`.
  It no longer requires `EnemyService` or `CombatService`.
  - **Init:** in mission mode only:
    - `CrowdService.OnKilled(onCrowdKilled)`
    - `ArenaService.SetShareSource` (run damage map)
    - `ArenaService.SetDownSource(VitalsService.IsDown by userId)`
    - `ArenaService.SetCharacterHook(WeaponService.PrepareCharacter)`
    - `WeaponService.SetActGate`
    - `ArenaService.SetResetHook(WaveService.Reset)`
  - **Spawning:** rulings 15–17.
  - **Wave clear:** the queue is empty and `CrowdService.AliveCount() == 0`. **Added
    2026-10-13 (second review):** the clear calls `VitalsService.ClearThreats()` first, then
    flushes, then stands the downed up, also on the last wave.
  - **Phase:** `"boss"` while the boss body lives.
  - **`onCrowdKilled(id, byUserId, info)`:**
    - adds `Combat.CrowdReward(mission, info.kind, spec)` to the pool;
    - adds `info.damageBy` to the flush tally and the run map;
    - counts the kill for `byUserId` when it is a member;
    - stamps the tempo;
    - when `info.boss`, adds the boss's `valor × rewardMult` and pushes `bossDown`.
  - The flush, `ContributionShares`, `SplitPool`, `CombatCashMult`, `payMentors`, the mission
    record and the snapshot are unchanged.
  - **`EndRun`:** `CrowdService.Clear()`, `VitalsService.ClearThreats()`,
    `WeaponService.AbandonProjectiles()`, then as today.
  - **Breather:** no flat breather regen in crowd missions (`VitalsService` regen is the only
    healing). At every wave boundary, downed members stand up (ruling 18).
  - **New public functions:** `WaveService.OnDown(player)` (ruling 18) and

- **`DebugService.luau`**: ruling 25, plus the lever `skip`. The bot tick is a no-op in crowd

- **`Main.server.luau`**: the boot sequence above.
- **`src/shared/Combat.luau`** (pure; mirrored in `tools/sim_combat.py` by the economy-designer):
  ```luau
  export type CrowdWaveSpec = {
  	wave: number,
  	groups: { { kind: string, count: number } },   -- counts resolved for party size and Overdrive
  	total: number,                                -- sum of group counts (boss not included)
  	boss: Types.MissionCrowdBoss?,
  	bossHpMult: number,
  	hpScale: number, plateScale: number, damageScale: number, regenShare: number,
  	rewardMult: number,                           -- overdrive.rewardMult or 1
  }
  Combat.CrowdWave(mission, wave, partySize, overdrive, combatCfg): CrowdWaveSpec?  -- nil: no crowd block / no such wave
  Combat.CrowdReward(mission, kind, spec): (number, number)   -- round(cash*rewardMult), round(materials*rewardMult); unknown kind = 0, 0
  ```

  - Group count: `round(count × (1 + (perExtra or coop.countPerExtraPlayer) × extras) ×

### Client (ui-engineer)

- **One mode gate.** Every `CameraController.IsRange()` call site reads `CombatMode.Get()`.
  - `CrowdRenderer`, `FeedbackController`, `AbilityFx`, `ThreatFx`, `VitalsController` and
    `MovementController` run in **both** modes.
  - `InputController` uses its range bindings (`RequestRangeAttack` and the rest) in both modes.
    The C1 mission bindings stay unbound until Wave 3 deletes them.
  - `CameraController.IsRange()` stays as `CombatMode.Get() == "range"` for the range-only
    pieces.
- **`CameraController`**: ADS, the pivot lag and the leap follow apply in both modes. The phase
  rules (`camera.freeCursorPhases`) apply in missions only, as before.
- **`InputController`**: no attacks or abilities while the run phase is `lobby`, `summary` or
  `ended`, or while the player is down. The server refuses them anyway; this keeps the client from
  drawing swings that will be taken back. **Corrected 2026-10-13 (second review):** also not
  while the local member waits on the pad for the next wave, and the same rule gates the slot
  switch. It is one predicate, `InputController.CanAct()`, fed by
  `InputController.SetPhase(phase, waiting)`; the HUD veils its ability tiles by it.
- **`CombatUIController`**: a third boot, `bootMission`. It mounts the range HUD pieces
  (`Crosshair`, the Feedback overlay, `AbilityBar`, the `VitalsHud`, `BossBar`, the range's touch
  buttons) and the run layer of `CombatHud`: wave and phase banner, breather timer, wallet, party
  list, Ready/Leave, `SummaryCard`, the safe-mode card.
  - `CombatHud` gains a `deps` flag (for example `actions = false`) that leaves out its
    Attack/stance/ability cluster, its HP bar and its boss bar.
  - The Studio-only `B` / `N` keys and their corner hint (above) live here.
  - `RangePanel` is range-only.
- **`VitalsHud` / `VitalsController`**: a `hurt` with `down = true` and no `upAt` shows a "DOWN"
  banner with no countdown. Solo, the summary card follows within a frame or two. **Added
  2026-10-13 (second review):** the mission down follows `PartyMember.down` in both directions
  (`VitalsController.SetServerDown`), each after a 1 s slack, and a held down survives a new
  character.
- **`CombatFxController`**: unchanged; it keeps `wave`, `bossDown` and `mentor`. Verify it
  ignores the range kinds as today.
- **Locals.** `FeedbackController` (159) and `CrowdRenderer` (151): group their state into tables
  before adding anything. Prefer new behaviour in new modules. `py tools/check_compile.py` is in
  every verify.
- `src/client/UI/Theme.luau`: add only.

### Types (applied verbatim by luau-engineer B in `src/shared/Types.luau`)

```luau
-- P5 wave 1 (docs/INTERFACES.md "P5 contracts")
export type CombatMode = "range" | "mission"

-- Missions/<n>_<Era>.json `crowd` block. Counts are per solo run; party size scales them
-- (Combat.CrowdWave). Scales multiply ProvingGrounds.json's tier-1 kind numbers.
export type MissionCrowdGroup = { kind: string, count: number, perExtra: number? }
export type MissionCrowdBoss = { kind: string, at: { number }, valor: number }  -- at = { x, z }
export type MissionCrowdWave = { groups: { MissionCrowdGroup }, boss: MissionCrowdBoss? }
export type MissionCrowdReward = { cash: number, materials: number }
export type MissionCrowdConfig = {
	hpScale: number,
	plateScale: number,
	damageScale: number,
	regenShare: number,
	maxAlive: number,
	burst: number,
	burstSpacing: number,
	eliteKind: string?,
	waves: { MissionCrowdWave },
	rewards: { [string]: MissionCrowdReward },
}
-- MissionConfig gains:
--	crowd: MissionCrowdConfig?,

-- Combat.json `crowdSkeleton` (ruling 2): wave i may hold the kinds introduced in waves 1..i
-- (bosses excepted) and must hold its own `introduces`.
export type CrowdSkeletonWave = { introduces: { string }, boss: string? }
-- CombatConfig gains:
--	crowdSkeleton: { CrowdSkeletonWave },

-- CombatDebugConfig gains:
--	provingBoots: string,          -- "mission" | "range"
--	provingMission: string,
--	provingStartWave: number,
--	provingStartDelay: number,
--	provingGear: { melee: number, ranged: number, ascension: { melee: number, ranged: number }? }?,
--	perfLogSeconds: number,

-- PartyMember gains:
--	down: boolean,                 -- ruling 18; false for bots
```

`CrowdWaveSpec` lives in `Combat.luau`; `CrowdScales` and `CrowdKillInfo` in `CrowdService`;
`MissionRules` in `VitalsService`. They are exported from their modules, not from `Types`.

### Config (economy-designer owns the files; the shapes are fixed here)

`Combat.json`:

```json
"crowdSkeleton": [
	{ "introduces": ["fodder"] },
	{ "introduces": [] },
	{ "introduces": ["slinger"] },
	{ "introduces": ["brute"] },
	{ "introduces": [], "boss": "colossus" },
	{ "introduces": ["marksman", "lobber"] },
	{ "introduces": [] },
	{ "introduces": ["armoured"] },
	{ "introduces": [] },
	{ "introduces": [], "boss": "warlord" }
],
"debug": { "...existing keys...",
	"provingBoots": "mission", "provingMission": "village", "provingStartWave": 1,
	"provingStartDelay": 3, "provingGear": { "melee": 2, "ranged": 1 }, "perfLogSeconds": 10 }
```

`Missions/1_Village.json` gains a `crowd` block. The old `enemies`, `waveTable` and `bosses`
blocks stay untouched until Wave 3. `waves`, `bossWaves`, `recommendedPower` and `targetMinutes`
keep their meaning; `targetWaveSeconds` is re-tuned for crowds.

```json
"crowd": {
	"hpScale": 0, "plateScale": 0, "damageScale": 0, "regenShare": 0,
	"maxAlive": 0, "burst": 0, "burstSpacing": 0,
	"waves": [
		{ "groups": [{ "kind": "fodder", "count": 0 }] },
		"... ten entries, one per skeleton wave ...",
		{ "groups": [], "boss": { "kind": "colossus", "at": [0, 0], "valor": 10 } },
		"...",
		{ "groups": [], "boss": { "kind": "warlord", "at": [0, 0], "valor": 25 } }
	],
	"rewards": {
		"fodder": { "cash": 0, "materials": 0 }, "slinger": {}, "brute": {}, "marksman": {},
		"lobber": {}, "armoured": {}, "guard": {}, "colossus": {}, "warlord": {}
	}
}
```

The zeros are placeholders for the designer's values. Valor stays 10 + 25 = 35. `boss.at` must
lie inside the 110 × 110 floor less the kind's radius. `ProvingGrounds.json` needs no change in
Wave 1. If tuning a mission needs a kind number changed, the range and both bosses must be
re-checked (`sim_range.py --check`).

**Corrected 2026-10-13 (second review):** `ProvingGrounds.json` gained one key,
`shooting.originSpeedSeconds` (0.1). No kind or weapon number changed. `Combat.json` gained
`player.rescue` and `director.runCapSeconds` went from 1200 to 1800. The Village arena layout
gained `wall.barrierHeight` and `wall.barrierThickness`. Shapes are in "Second review round
(2026-10-13)".

### Balance bands (economy-designer; checked by the simulators, written up in `docs/BALANCE.md` "P5")

All bands are at recommended power: gear 2/1, ascension 0, the range's default loadout
(Broadsword + Longbow), solo, no Overdrive.

- **Rewards per full run** (all ten waves, boss summons included at the count `sim_range.py`
  reports for the reacting player's boss fights):
  - cash within ±10% of **142,185**;
  - Timber within ±10% of **256**;
  - Valor exactly **35**.

  This holds even though the kills are 5–10× today's. Cash is before `CombatCashMult`, as in
  BALANCE's table.
- **Clear time:** a reacting player clears all ten waves in **10–15 minutes**, breathers
  included. The method (per-wave spawn time against kill time from `sim_range.py`'s DPS) is
  documented in BALANCE.
- **Bosses at Village scales:**
  - the **Colossus** with the default sword takes **64–90 s** (Ben called about 76 s "about
    right");
  - the **Warlord** takes **77–101 s** (guard, plate, duel as in Stop 3).
  - Expect `hpScale` ≈ the melee `DamageScale` at gear 2/1 (×1.5), which keeps the range's hits
    to kill.
- **Threat at recommended health** (145):
  - no single enemy hit over 25% of the bar;
  - a player standing still in a fodder wave goes down in 6–12 s;
  - `regenShare` close to the range's 10/130 a second.
- **Gates:**
  - every kind a wave can field (summons `fodder` and `guard` included) has a `rewards` entry;
  - every wave matches `crowdSkeleton`;
  - `#crowd.waves == waves`, and `bossWaves` equals the indices with a boss;
  - `boss.at` lies inside the floor.

### Remotes

**None new, none removed.** Ruling 20 lists what changes in use. `RequestDebug` gains the lever
string `skip` (value `"next"` or `"boss"`); its validator already admits it. `CombatFx` carries
the same kinds as P4, plus `wave`, `bossDown` and `mentor` from `RunFx`. `hurt.upAt` is absent in
missions. `RunState` is unchanged except `PartyMember.down`.
